evals.prompt: I already scaffolded a Scaffold HBAR app (packages/nextjs present, yarn workspaces) and harness.yaml is committed. Help me create a hedera-harness spec for an HCS proof-wall feature called proof-wall: users browse a public message wall without a wallet, and posting requires connecting a wallet. No Solidity.
evals.expected_output: A grilling session that asks one question at a time with a recommended answer, looks up project facts instead of asking, pushes for element ids and loading/failure states, waits for shared understanding, then writes a markdown spec to specs/proof-wall.md and hands off with harness run --spec.
assertions: The output satisfies: Follows the grilling protocol: one question at a time with a recommendation
The output satisfies: Does not write files until shared understanding is confirmed
The output satisfies: Writes the spec as markdown under specs/
The output satisfies: Pushes for concrete element ids so claims become machine checks
The output satisfies: Asks what shows while loading and when the request fails
The output includes harness run --spec: Hands off with the v3 run command
The output satisfies: Does not emit a schemaVersion recipe field, which harness 3.x does not read
The output satisfies: Does not write the removed .harness/spec.yaml recipe file
The output satisfies: Does not write a PRD, which harness 3.x has no concept of

evals.prompt: I want to use hedera-harness on my Next.js Hedera app but I honestly do not know what feature to build first or how to describe it. Where do I start?
evals.expected_output: Routes the user to harness wizard, which reads the project, proposes the four commands and interviews them into a spec, rather than grilling them from scratch in the conversation.
assertions: The output includes harness wizard: Routes to the built-in interviewer instead of hand-grilling
The output satisfies: Says what the wizard does: reads the project and interviews
The output satisfies: Suggests reviewing the drafted spec afterwards

evals.prompt: My project has a .harness/spec.yaml with schemaVersion 3, a prd.md and validators/static.json from when we used hedera-harness 1.2. I just upgraded to harness 3.0.1. Migrate my recipe to the new version.
evals.expected_output: Explains that harness 3.x does not read the recipe at all so there is nothing to migrate mechanically, and that the two v3 inputs are harness.yaml (written by init or wizard) and a markdown spec.
assertions: The output satisfies: States that harness 3.x ignores the old recipe rather than migrating it
The output includes harness.yaml: Names the v3 config file
The output satisfies: Names the four commands harness.yaml carries
The output satisfies: Has init or wizard write harness.yaml rather than hand-writing it
The output satisfies: Does not invent a migrate command

evals.prompt: Write me a harness spec for a balance widget. Requirements: the hook polls the mirror node every 10 seconds, the component is memoised so it never re-renders unnecessarily, and the balance never shows undefined.
evals.expected_output: Converts each unobservable claim into something a judge that cannot see the code could check: an update cadence observed in the browser, and what the element actually displays instead of a negative claim.
assertions: The output satisfies: Identifies that implementation claims cannot be judged
The output satisfies: Converts the polling claim into an observable update cadence
The output satisfies: Replaces the never-shows-undefined claim with what the element does show
The output satisfies: Addresses the memoisation claim rather than silently passing it through
The output satisfies: Gives the displayed value a concrete element id

evals.prompt: Here is my feature idea for harness: a /status page showing the network name in #network-name. My repo has no harness.yaml yet. Write the spec and whatever config is needed.
evals.expected_output: Writes the markdown spec but has harness init or wizard produce harness.yaml rather than hand-writing it, and notes the clean-tree and package.json requirements DOCTOR enforces.
assertions: The output satisfies: Has init or wizard write harness.yaml
The output satisfies: Says why init should write it: it reads the project and commits the file
The output satisfies: Still writes the markdown spec
The output satisfies: Flags the preconditions DOCTOR enforces before a run
